Nineteen comments

Paddy Mill’s Fancy

This one is for Gian Marco, as we’ve both recently posted a tune from Desi Wilkinson’s“Three Piece Flute” recording. This fine reel is on it too. Tara Diamond, a great flute-player from Belfast, taught this to a Willie Clancy flute class in the mid-80s.Not only that, but she also got hold of the composer, fiddle-player Paddy Mills from Mayo, who was around that week, and got him to come along to the class to play us his original version, which is the version I have posted. It is a popular session tune in Ireland these days, especially with flute-players, but I’m not sure if it’s that well-known abroad.
As well as Desi, “Skylark” and concertina player Terry Bingham have recorded it, although they all have slightly different versions of the tune. Beware in sessions - sometimes the 2nd part the 2nd time round goes back to the last 4 bars of the first part- if that makes sense (Skylark play it like that )- but that’s not how the composer played it to the class. Enjoy!

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 21st, 2003.

M:4/4
K:G
DGGF GBAG|FGAB c2Bc|d2eg fdcA|AGFA GFEF|

:g2dg gedc|BG~G2 FGAB|c3A dcAG|FGAB cdef|
g2dg gedc|BG~G2 FGAB|c3A dcAG|FGAF DGG2|
g2dg gedc|BG~G2 FGAB|c3A dcAG|FGAG FGEF|
DGGF GBAG|FGAB c2Bc|d2eg fdcA|AGFA G3F||

This version, instead of repeating the B-part, reverts to the second strain of the A-part for lthe last 8 bars.

I had the pleasure of meeting Paddy Mills last year in Milltown Malbay. Knowing his name, but not much else about him, I played him the above version of the tune. His face lit up and he began playing along - I noticed that he played the B-part differently. I told him I had got the tune form Skylark, to which he replied, “Yes, they got it wrong.” He wrote them a letter to tell them and they sent back a letter of apology.

So, if you ever meet Mr.Mills, don’t play the setting I’ve just posted.

https://musicofmayo.ie/paddy-mills-fancy/

The tune’s original title is ‘Paddy Mills’ Dream’.

Transcribed from recording of the tunes composer, Paddy Mills (Barr na Trá, Belmullet) in Fidiléirí – Mayo Fiddlers.

Although nowadays this tune is more commonly called Paddy Mills’ Fancy/Delight, it was originally known by the above title and came about at Corraun House during an informal cultural school initiated there by Castlebar musician John Hoban in the early/mid 1980s:

“It happened this way. I woke up one morning with the tune ringing in my head. So I got up and played it over and over. I didn’t play it out for about six months to see if anyone else had it because I thought maybe I had it brought with me from a session, unknown to me”.1

Joe Byrne, Fidiléirí – Mayo Fiddlers. Dreoilín Community Arts, Achadh Mór, (Book and double Cassette), 1995, p23.
